situation:
You are to assume the role of promotion manager at STARFIELD OPEN AIR CINEMAS, an operator of drive-in and outdoor cinemas across a four-county region. The vice president of marketing (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should answer a naming rights offer that arrived last week, and to be ready to explain the thinking behind whichever direction you choose.

STARFIELD absorbed a smaller drive-in circuit eight months ago and has not finished digesting it. Six of the acquired fields still carry their old marquee name, the two ticketing sites still sell separately, and regulars at each field talk about the company as if it were still two businesses. Half the territory knows STARFIELD for cheap family nights; the other half knows it for premium double features.

VALLEY HARVEST MARKETS, a regional grocery chain, has offered a five-year naming rights agreement for the flagship field. Signing that agreement would pay for a laser projection upgrade and a wider concession menu, and the grocery chain would promote the venue in its stores and its weekly circular. The payment covers that upgrade only if attendance next summer grows the way the company's own forecast projects; if the forecast misses, STARFIELD carries the balance of the projector loan itself.

Declining the offer would leave the STARFIELD name alone on the flagship marquee while the acquired fields are finally renamed. It would also mean funding a smaller upgrade by raising ticket prices, which regulars at the acquired fields have already complained to staff about, and running the aging projectors for two more seasons. The vice president (judge) wants your recommendation and the positioning that should follow it.

Be ready to describe how you would position the flagship field afterward, the word-of-mouth channels the company relies on, the public relations channels it would use to announce the decision, and what the concession product mix should carry. The vice president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
